summary:
Turn 61 reviewed the codec finding's second scenario, which turns the truncation into a framing failure for everything that follows.

State on entry. The first C10 artifact is confirmed (a 70000-byte value is written as 70013 bytes but decoded as 4464 with 4477 consumed). The second artifact, 1f0944699e7d4301909aa30f0523e9b5 (executed as 8628f4fc…), reported violated with the oracle correspondence unreviewed, and its retained stream shows the follow-on command decoded as op 197, an arbitrary key and a 53198-byte value with 12341 bytes left in the buffer.

Review judgement (checker_correspondence, no_issue_found). Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a value the client can build must survive the codec, and this scenario asserts that the command following such a value still decodes to what was written; the run reports second_matches false with the decoded fields printed, so the assertion is evaluated on the decoder's own output. Entry and legality: two Command marshallings in one buffer is how the durable recorder appends commands — each written in sequence with no per-command framing — which is exactly the consecutive-decode shape the scenario needs, and that framing detail is stated as the exercised input rather than blurred. Oracle and identity: second_matches compares the decoded fields with what the harness wrote, and the stream identity correlates prerequisite and result, so the garbage values are attributable to the shift rather than to correlation. Limits are explicit: the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary; no replica reader consumes the shifted stream, so the reader's own reaction (an unknown message type once the framing is lost) is unobserved; and a message's array framing, which would be corrupted the same way because the decoder trusts the value length, is not the exercised input.

Effect on the run's picture. C10 now stands as a two-scenario obligation — the value truncation itself and the framing failure it inflicts on the following command — with its importance bounded by the configured command size but its mechanism fully recorded. Audit spec version 13; the nine earlier settled claims (C1/C6/C7/C9 confirmed violations, C2/C3/C4 confirmed, C5/C8 bounded protections) and the two paused candidates are untouched, with the scope-issue bookkeeping on the superseded C1 artifact the only visible administrative item. No requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
